thread.title: Stock Indexes Sails Ahead On 3 Economic Reports | Investor's Business Daily

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Stock Indexes Sails Ahead On 3 Economic Reports | Investor's Business Daily
text:
U.S. stock indexes advanced late Wednesday morning as the Nasdaq headed toward its best price and volume action in nine sessions. Three financial reports pointed to a strengthening economy.
X The Nasdaq popped 0.4% while the Dow Jones industrial average and the S&P 500 posted gains of 0.4% to 0.5%. Small caps surged as the Russell 2000 added 0.5%.
Volume was slightly higher on the NYSE vs. the same time Tuesday. Trade on the Nasdaq, however, ran about 20% faster than the prior day.
Apple ( AAPL ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ) rose 1.7% and 0.6% respectively. Amazon.com ( AMZN ) added 0.9% early but then reversed to a 0.3% loss. Volume was 35% above normal for Apple, 70% heavier for Amazon and below average for Microsoft.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Stock Indexes: These 3 Are Giants In The Nasdaq The three stocks are the biggest weightings in the Nasdaq, together accounting for 20% of the index. Apple and Microsoft scored new highs Wednesday.
New highs, combining the NYSE and Nasdaq, have been a problem recently. In six of the past seven sessions, not including Wednesday, new lows outnumbered new highs. The market was on track for new lows to lead again Wednesday.
The day's leaders in the IBD 50, a proxy for top-rated stocks, included Apple; digital advertising firm Trade Desk ( TTD ), 3% in heavy volume; and restaurant chain Wingstop ( WING ), up 2.5% in brisk trade.
Big losers included Ligand Pharmaceuticals ( LGND ), down 5% in heavy volume.
Financial News Economic reports were bullish. The employment report from Automated Data Processing showed payrolls in September hit 230,000 . The figure surpassed the entire range of estimates.
The Purchasing Managers Index for services in September rolled in at 53.5, topping the consensus view for 52.9.
September data for the Institute for Supply Management came in at 61.6 for the services sector, beating views for 58.
